Get the nodes that JAGS monitors

Source: R/helpfunctions_JAGS.R
get_monitor_nodes.Rd

Temporary, until rjags is fixed: rjags >= 5 (checked with rjags 5-5 and 5-6) cannot set a monitor on an element of a node whose name contains an underscore, letters and another underscore (e.g., D_y_id[1,2], the covariance matrix of the random effects of y on the level id); it warns "Failed to set value trace monitor". The cause is in parse.varnames() of rjags, which takes such names for reserved names (like "_observed_") and does not split them into node and index. The whole node can be monitored. With rjags >= 5, such elements are therefore replaced by their node, and select_monitored_columns() keeps the requested elements. Other names (e.g., beta, M_lvlone[3,2]) are monitored as they are. Monitoring whole nodes costs time for large nodes (e.g., the random effects of all subjects), so it is only done with rjags >= 5.

Usage

get_monitor_nodes(var_names,
  whole_nodes = numeric_version(getNamespaceVersion("rjags")) >= "5.0")

Arguments

var_names

a character vector with the names of the nodes and elements to monitor (e.g., "beta", "D_y_id[1,2]")

whole_nodes

logical; whether the affected elements are replaced by their node (by default with rjags >= 5)

Value

a character vector with the names to give to JAGS: var_names, with the affected elements replaced by the name of their node (each node once) if whole_nodes is TRUE, otherwise var_names
